t:
(a) 
The second sentence of section 5597(e) of title 10, United States Code, is amended to read as follows: “Such appointments shall be made by the President alone, except that appointments under subsections (f) and (g) in grades above lieutenant commander in the Navy shall be made by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.”
 
    (b) 
The second sentence of section 5787(e) of such title is amended to read as follows: “Each such appointment to a grade above lieutenant commander in the Navy or to a grade above major in the Marine Corps shall be made by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.”
 
    (c) 
The first sentence of section 5791(b) of such title is amended to read as follows: “Permanent and temporary appointments under this chapter in a grade above lieutenant commander in the Naval Reserve and in a grade above major in the Marine Corps Reserve shall be made by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.”
 
    (d) The first sentence of section 5912 of such title is amended to read as follows: “Permanent and temporary appointments under this chapter in grades above lieutenant commander in the Naval Reserve and in grades above major in the Marine Corps Reserve shall be made by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.”

fable.w: The section only amends who appoints Navy and Marine Corps officers above certain grades, requiring presidential appointment with Senate advice and consent. The tempting reading is that "advice and consent" is a form of consultation, but the Senate is part of Congress and so inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is involved in any federal decision here.
fable.s: shall be made by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate

opus.w: The only interaction here is the Senate's advice and consent on military appointments. The Senate is part of Congress, so it is inside the federal government. "Advice and consent" can sound like a consultation process, but no state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public takes part in these appointment decisions.
opus.s: shall be made by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes the appointment process for military officers, requiring the advice and consent of the Senate. The definition explicitly states that Congress and its members are inside the federal government. Therefore, the interaction between the President and the Senate is intra-governmental and does not constitute participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: “Such appointments shall be made by the President alone, except that appointments under subsections (f) and (g) in grades above lieutenant commander in the Navy shall be made by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "advice and consent of the Senate" constitutes participation because the Senate is involved in the decision. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress, its committees, and its members are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, interaction between the President and the Senate is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
